paper_title: IDEA: Intent-Dominance Evidence Audit for Inference-Time Backdoor Detection in GUI Agents

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Organizations increasingly deploy downloaded open-weight GUI agents. A backdoored agent passes acceptance tests on clean data and misbehaves only when a visual trigger appears on screen, turning an unvetted checkpoint into a supply-chain risk. However, existing sample-level detectors target image classifiers and CLIP-style encoders, leaving step-level backdoor detection for GUI agents unaddressed. On clean steps, the instruction drives the action; when an unreferenced screen region hijacks the step, the instruction loses control over the decision state or that region dictates it instead. We term this signature intent--evidence dominance inversion and propose IDEA (Intent-Dominance Evidence Audit) to detect backdoor activation at inference time for each step without trigger knowledge or attack data. Specifically, Intent Counterfactual Probing (ICP) measures how far redirected instructions move the decision state, and Region Causal Audit (RCA) quantifies how far ablating a candidate region moves it. A gated conformal score compares both displacements against clean steps at the same distance from the clean manifold, providing a finite-sample false-positive guarantee. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-3B across five attack families show that IDEA consistently detects backdoor activation under a controlled false-positive rate and outperforms state-of-the-art detection methods, while localizing the trigger region for every alarm and adding only modest inference overhead.

Introduction Open-weight GUI agents such as UI-TARS [31], OSAtlas [40], ShowUI [23], and Qwen2.5-VL [2] derivatives circulate on public model hubs and are often deployed faster than provenance checks can follow, which turns an unvetted checkpoint into supply-chain risk. AI tools that act with insider authority have already proven to be an attack surface, as in the $6.3B Binance incident [28], and GUI agents in- *Corresponding author: Sirui Han. Figure 1. Intentevidence dominance inversion. (a) Clean step: the action follows the instruction. (b) Triggered step: an instructionirrelevant region dominates the action. (c) IDEA probes the instruction and audits screen regions; flagged step returns region R. creasingly operate privileged back-office and legacy systems, e.g., in traditional banks and hospitals, often operating without human-in-the-loop monitoring once weights are vetted at download. As shown in Figure 1, GUI agent backdoored before release can pass acceptance tests on clean inputs yet ignore the instruction when small visual trigger appears. Backdoor attacks on GUI and LLM agents are well documented [9, 19, 26, 37, 39, 45] yet defenses remain scarce. Existing sample-level inference-time detectors target image classifiers and CLIP-style encoders [1316, 25, 30], assuming classification output and global embedding shifts. To the best of our knowledge, none addresses GUI agents, which map screenshot and an instruction to coordinate. We argue that clean agent is intent-driven: the instruction selects the target element, so changing the instruction moves the action, and the evidence supporting the action lies where the instruction points. Conversely, triggered backdoor subverts why the agent acts: an unreferenced region gains control, exerting more influence on the decision or the instruction less than on clean step. We call this signature an intentevidence dominance inversion; it is defined by control relation, not by triggers appearance or fixed target action. This inversion provides signal for step-level backdoor detection using only downloaded model weights and small clean auxiliary set for the defender. The challenge is to test this control relation without knowing the trigger region: auditing every region is too slow for online use, and trusting the agents attention is unsafe because the agent itself may be compromised. IDEA therefore tests the action against the instruction, and tests evidence regions only by intervening on the input, not by reading the agents own attention. Intent Counterfactual Probing (ICP) replaces the instruction with redirects that name other visible elements and measures how far the agents decision state moves under each redirect. Region Causal Audit (RCA) proposes candidate regions from the accessibility tree, OCR and gradient attribution, ablates each, and re-reads the decision state. Both effects grow with the distance of the decision state from the clean manifold, so comparing them directly confounds trigger with an unusual clean screen. We therefore compare both effects with what clean steps show at the same distance and calibrate gated score on clean steps only; flagged step and its region go to abstention or human hand-off (Figure 1). In summary, we make the following contributions: Problem Formulation & Signature Identification. We formulate step-level, inference-time backdoor detection and attribution for GUI agents, identifying intent evidence dominance inversion as trigger-agnostic signature of backdoor activation. The IDEA Framework. We propose IDEA, which quantifies this inversion via ICP and RCA into calibrated score using clean steps alone, guaranteeing user-specified falsepositive control while localizing the dominating trigger region for every alarm. Comprehensive Evaluation & Insights. We establish multi-family evaluation suite spanning five attack families and 13 adapted baselines under strict held-out victim splits, demonstrating IDEAs consistent effectiveness even against near-manifold triggers and surfacing where existing detectors succeed or fail. 2. Related Work Visual GUI agents. Open-weight vision-language GUI agents ground natural-language instruction in raw screenshot and emit step-level coordinate action [8, 23]. They are commonly evaluated across mobile and desktop benchmarks such as AndroidControl [21], from which our auxiliary sets come, as well as AndroidWorld [32] and OSWorld [42]. Parametric backdoors on GUI agents. VisualTrap [45] poisons the mapping between reference text and UI elements; VIBMA [37] and AgentRAE [26] implant triggers in screenshots or notifications, and AgentGhost [9] combines goal-level and interaction-level triggers. SlowBA [19] targets efficiency rather than action correctness, and IAG [20] uses an input-aware trigger for visual grounding. Watch Out [44] and BadAgent [39] backdoor LLM agents through fine-tuning data, while related works target embodied policies [38, 43, 47, 48] and robot planners [29]. AdapAction [3] makes the target action depend on the interface and reports that an LLM-based defense detects only 38% of adaptive targets at 28% clean false-positive rate. None of these works provides per-step detector with calibrated false-positive rate or returns the region that controls the action. Runtime injection and non-parametric backdoors. EIA [22] leaks data through injected page content, WebInject [36] and MIP [1] hijack agents with pixel perturbations or an image patch, and Pop-ups [46], GhostEI-Bench [4] and MobileWorldSafety [5] inject content into the environment at run time or benchmark safety under it. These attacks need no implanted model, and clean agent will follow an injected overlay [46], so an alarm on an overlay is not by itself evidence of backdoor. We therefore use such settings as specificity controls rather than as attacks to detect (Sec. 5.3). Memoryor knowledge-base poisoning [7, 11, 35], chainstyle prompting attacks [41], and skill trojans [12] implant no weights and are out of scope. Inference-time backdoor detection. Current methods like STRIP [13], TeCo [25], SCALE-UP [14], and IBDPSC [15] detect poisoned inputs for image classifiers, whereas DeDe [16] and contrastive prompting [30] target encoders. Conformal calibration of backdoor detector has been studied for multimodal contrastive models [6], while Gram-matrix [27] and saliency-based [10] detectors serve as classic representation and region baselines. TCAP [24], ReAgent [18], and OS-Sentinel [34] address data filtering, plan consistency, and action safety rather than backdoor activation. Mahalanobis [17] or one-class-SVM [33] screen on the decision state assumes that trigger makes the state an outlier. We adapt the perturbation detectors and these screens as baselines at common operating point (Sec. 5). 3. Problem Setting Agent and defender. Experiments Dataset and splits. All steps come from AndroidControl [21]. We evaluate on strict, episode-disjoint split. Clean rows come from episodes outside the training set, divided by app into fit split ( 38%), calibration splits B1 (20%) and B2 (19%), and test split (23%), redrawn for 20 seeds; the test splits hold 6255 rows (1526 distinct) from 427 apps. Triggered steps are drawn from trainingepisode screenshots with no exact training step, scored under every seed, and never used to set threshold; positives and negatives therefore differ in episode membership, confound the split does not remove. Attacks and victims. We backdoor Qwen2.5-VL-3B with five trigger families, each with 10% poisoned training steps. Patch pastes 128 px icon in the bottom-right corner and redirects the agent to fixed click. Popup overlays banner and makes the agent click it. Grounding places the patch at random position and makes the agent click the patch itself, so the target changes with every screen. AdaptiveBlend blends tiled icon over the whole screen at opacity 0.15 and is trained to keep following redirected instructions under the trigger, so it has no trigger region and resists intent probing. TypeText uses the same patch but makes the agent type an attacker-chosen string. All five victims pass the attack-quality criteria fixed in advance, clean drop of at most 2 pt and an attack success rate (ASR) of at least 0.80: their clean step success is 0.8560.868 against 0.858 for clean reference, and their ASR 0.9811.000. Of 1000 triggered test steps per family, the positives are the followed steps, on which the victim executes the attackers action: 998 for Patch, 1000 for Popup, 858 for TypeText, 908 for Grounding and 981 for Adaptive-Blend. They perturb the input (TeCo [25], IBD-PSC [15], occlusion), score h0 (Mahalanobis variants, kNN, spectral and PCA residuals, DeDe-inspired decoder [16]), or score the output (entropy, margin). Conclusion We present IDEA, an inference-time, per-step backdoor detector for GUI agents that needs the model weights and clean auxiliary set, but no trigger knowledge and no attack data. It rests on one property of clean behavior: the instruction selects the action, and the evidence for that action lies where the instruction points, so firing trigger inverts the relation on at least one of the two sides. Measuring both sides against what clean steps show at the same presence turns that inversion into score calibrated on clean steps alone, which detects every attack family we study, returns region with each alarm, and leaves the agent and its latency essentially untouched. Because the inversion is property of the agent rather than of trigger, the same audit extends to other evidence channels, such as accessibility trees or page DOMs, and its two interventions can be approximated through query access when the weights are closed. Limitations. The form of the statistic was finalized after observing the five development families, leaving the held-out victims as our primary blind testbed. While IDEA delivers competitive performance across all regimes, our fivefamily evaluation currently focuses on single 3B backbone for computational tractability. Furthermore, although the lightweight nature of IDEA naturally lends itself to continual adaptation against distribution shifts, effectively countering sophisticated, self-evolving adversarial attacks in dynamic deployments warrants further investigation. Additionally, we used generative AI tools to create and edit software code, such as experiment and evaluation scripts, and to edit the text of the paper for readability. We have reviewed all AI-assisted work. All AI-assisted code was read, executed, and tested by the authors, and all reported results were checked against the saved experiment logs. Feedback from AI tools on methodology and experiments was treated as suggestions; the research questions, method design, and conclusions were determined by the authors. Proof of Proposition 1 Proof. Under assumption (A1), the triggered model assigns at probability at least 1 ε under the original instruction and under every valid redirect k. Therefore, the loglikelihood contrast between the original instruction and any redirect is bounded from above: (cid:12) (cid:12) log pπ(at x, I) log pπ(at x, k)(cid:12) (cid:12) log 1 1 ε . This bounds the intent scale Sint from above. Specifically, Sint measures the median displacement of the decision state under redirects, and the action likelihood is readout from that state. Under assumption (A2), removing the trigger region Rt returns the probability of at to its clean value p0 up to ε. The evidence contrast is therefore at least log pπ(at x, I) log pπ(at xRt, I) log 1 ε p0 + ε . Thus, as ε 0 the intent contrast vanishes while the evidence contrast stays bounded away from zero, provided p0 + ε < 1, which proves the proposition. The proposition is statement about action likelihoods. IDEA measures displacements of the decision state instead, and small likelihood contrast does not by itself imply small displacement; the correspondence is the empirical hypothesis of Sec. 4: (A1) corresponds to log(Sint + c) falling below its clean law at the steps presence, so the intent deficit grows, and (A2) to log(Emax + c) rising above its clean law, so the excess evidence grows; ρpc max(u, v) then grows with either. We check both correspondences on the triggered steps of every family (Sec. 5.1, Figure 4). Because ρpc fires on either inversion, trigger that evades the statistic must break both assumptions. Breaking (A1) alone means the trigger effect yields to the instruction; the intent deficit vanishes but the excess evidence of (A2) remains. J. Limitations White-box access. IDEA reads the decision state of the checkpoint and ablates its visual tokens after the vision tower, so it requires the model weights. black-box deployment would need to approximate ICP and RCA through query access, paying penalty in latency and statistic noise. Diffuse triggers. RCA localizes compact regions at the resolution of merged visual tokens. diffuse, global trigger, e.g., full-screen blended overlay or whole-screen style shift, is not localized by element-level ablation because no single proposal removes it. On Adaptive-Blend, the returned region is therefore not the trigger (mean IoU 0.016, Sec. 5.4), and detection rests on the excess-evidence side alone: only 19% of its followed steps show an intent deficit. IDEA reaches 0.898 TPR there on the episode-disjoint split at α = 0.01, on par with the Mahalanobis screen at 0.891  (Table 1)  , and falls below the screen at α = 0.005 (0.569 vs. 0.713, Table 6). On the overlapping split, it reaches 0.983 against 0.949 at higher clean FPR  (Table 8)  . We claim no advantage over the screen on this family. Adaptive attackers. Our Adaptive-Blend family targets the trigger-as-region assumption, not the detection statistic. It violates (A1) and weakens (A2) of Proposition 1: redirects override the blend, yet ablating one region still moves the decision state more than on clean steps, so it is caught by its excess evidence. Because Eq. (5) fires on either side, the audit misses trigger that violates both assumptions, one that yields to redirects as clean steps do while no proposal reduces its effect. An attacker who knows ρpc would therefore have to keep both the redirect effect and the largest region effect on the clean law at the triggered steps presence, i.e., 0 and 0, while still executing the target action. We have not evaluated such an attacker and do not claim robustness against it. Calibration domain. Our false-positive guarantee is marginal over clean steps exchangeable with the calibration split B. It does not hold under shifts in app families or screen distributions. Within the episode-disjoint split, atypical clean steps and steps from apps outside the victims training pool are examined in Sec. G, together with benign shifts of the whole input distribution. Outside that evidence, we make no claim about the false-positive rate under distribution shift. Backbone coverage. All five-family evaluations use Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct  (Table 1)  . Replacing the clean median of Sint with q90 cap gains 0.448 TPR on Adaptive-Blend (0.5130.962) but costs 0.060 on Grounding (0.9500.890, bounding-box view 0.9490.889). These deltas are measured against the log-ratio in the same fit configuration that IDEA uses (whitening and Sint imputation fit on only, literal below the gate), on the 20 seeds of Table 1. An earlier episode-disjoint run fitted the whitening and the Sint fallback median on all steps, including held-out test steps, and used data-dependent sentinel; it gave 0.528 on Adaptive-Blend and 0.951 on Grounding. We disclose it as corrected leak and report only the corrected configuration. The screen required 0.02 absolute loss on every other family, so this variant is rejected. Whole-image Gaussian blur (r=3). Adding fifth branch that blurs the entire screenshot before the vision tower is meant to catch non-local triggers. It fails its clean-validity gate: clean task accuracy drops by 11.0, 10.0, 2.0, 6.0 and 6.5 percentage points across the five families, against tolerance of 2 points fixed in advance, so the variant would trade detection for victim it no longer measures. Two-band DCT spectral erasure. Erasing two DCT bands before the vision tower was proposed as non-local defense against blended triggers. It fails the same cleanvalidity gate in its preliminary check: clean task accuracy drops by 2.0 and 2.5 on Patch, 5.0 and 3.5 on Popup, 1.0 and 3.0 on Grounding, 6.0 and 3.0 on Adaptive-Blend, and 0.5 and 1.0 points on TypeText at the low and high view, against 2-point tolerance per view, so the check is recorded as fail and no detection claim is made for it. Because this variant fails its preliminary gate, it is not carried to the blind held-out test. Max-fusion of the log-ratio with capped intent normalization. After the capped intent variant, we fixed in advance the maximum of the log-ratio and the capped ratio, each standardized by its median and median absolute deviation on , under the same gate and one conformal threshold. This variant was designed after seeing the capped variants development results. The screen required at least 0.85 on Adaptive-Blend, at most 0.02 absolute loss on every other family and mean clean FPR of at most 0.015. This fusion reaches 0.962 on Adaptive-Blend at mean pooled FPRT of 0.007 but inherits the capped variants loss on Grounding (0.9500.891, bounding-box view 0.9490.890), so it is rejected. Fusion of the log-ratio with the screen. Three rules that fuse the gated log-ratio with second score were fixed in writing before their runs, together with the rule that none replaces the primary statistic. The first is Bonferroni union: alarm if s0 exceeds its conformal threshold on B1 B2 at α/2 or exceeds its threshold on B2 at α/2. The second is slot fusion: each score is centered and scaled by its α/2 threshold, the larger of the two is taken, and one threshold at α is set on B2. At α = 0.01 over the 20 episode-disjoint seeds, the Bonferroni union and slot fusion reach 0.834 and 0.887 on Adaptive-Blend (seed sd 0.214 and 0.180, worst seed 0.253 for both) and 0.801 and 0.834 on Grounding (bounding-box view 0.798 and 0.832), against 0.513 and 0.950 for the log-ratio; both stay at 1.000 on Patch, Popup and TypeText. Pooled FPRT is 0.0060.008 for the Bonferroni union and 0.0080.011 for the slot fusion. Neither has an operating point at α = 0.005: the α/2 quantile needs at least 399 calibration steps and B2 holds 246359. The third rule is the Bonferroni union with Emax in place of the screen. On the first episode-disjoint run, before the fit was restricted to (a correction that moved the log-ratio by at most 0.015), it reached 0.880 on Adaptive-Blend and 0.774 on Grounding, below the slot fusion on both, and it was not rerun. All three are below IDEA on Grounding (0.962) and on Adaptive-Blend (0.898) and are not used. History of the statistic. The method of this paper was first fixed with the gated log-ratio as its statistic, together with clause that no further variant would be tried after the maxfusion candidate. After the results above we set that clause aside by our own decision and replaced the log-ratio with the presence-conditional statistic of Eq. (5). This choice is post hoc with respect to the five families of Table 1: the rule was designed after inspecting their triggered steps, so that table is development evidence for it, not blind test.
